% =============================================================================
% Grease fire  -  companions burn flammable enemies by igniting oil under them
% =============================================================================
% Fire only matters on oil: igniting an oiled area makes it ablaze for good, and
% every flammable enemy standing in an ablaze area is burned. Burned is derived,
% never stored, so one fire takes every flammable enemy in its area along.
%
% burnOut(?e) enumerates every way to burn one enemy, for every companion and
% skill that can do each step (plain alternatives, no else):
%   1. ignite the oiled area the enemy stands in;
%   2. spill oil under the enemy, then ignite it;
%   3. lure the enemy into a linked oiled area that is not ablaze, then ignite it.
% clear burns the flammable enemies one at a time, in enemy/1 order.

% =============================================================================
% OPERATORS
% =============================================================================

opMoveTo(?who, ?from, ?to) :- del(at(?who, ?from)), add(at(?who, ?to)).
opSpend(?who, ?skill, ?old, ?new) :- del(charges(?who, ?skill, ?old)), add(charges(?who, ?skill, ?new)).
opSpill(?who, ?skill, ?area) :- del(), add(oiled(?area)).
opIgnite(?who, ?skill, ?area) :- del(), add(ablaze(?area)).
opLure(?who, ?skill, ?e) :- del(), add(lured(?e, ?who)).
opChase(?e, ?from, ?to) :- del(at(?e, ?from)), add(at(?e, ?to)).

% =============================================================================
% RULES
% =============================================================================

% A flammable enemy in an ablaze area is burned.
burned(?e) :- flammable(?e), at(?e, ?area), ablaze(?area).

% The flammable enemies clear still has to burn, in enemy/1 order.
unburned(?e) :- enemy(?e), flammable(?e), not(burned(?e)).

% A companion able to use a skill of ?element right now: it knows the skill and
% has a charge left. ?new is the charge count after one use.
canUse(?c, ?skill, ?element, ?old, ?new) :-
    companion(?c), knows(?c, ?skill), skillElement(?skill, ?element),
    charges(?c, ?skill, ?old), >(?old, 0), is(?new, -(?old, 1)).

% =============================================================================
% METHODS - clear
% =============================================================================

% Burn the first unburned flammable enemy, then look again: a fire may have
% taken later enemies along.
clear :-
    if(first(unburned(?e))),
    do(burnOut(?e), clear).

% Nothing left to burn. Negated rather than else, so a failed burnOut above
% cannot fall through to an empty plan.
clear :-
    if(not(unburned(?e))),
    do().

% =============================================================================
% METHODS - burnOut
% =============================================================================

% 1. Ignite: the enemy already stands on oil.
burnOut(?e) :-
    if(at(?e, ?area), oiled(?area)),
    do(ignite(?area)).

% 2. Spill and ignite: oil the enemy's area, then set it on fire.
burnOut(?e) :-
    if(at(?e, ?area), not(oiled(?area))),
    do(spill(?area), ignite(?area)).

% 3. Lure into oil: draw the enemy into a linked oiled area that is not yet
%    ablaze, then set that area on fire.
burnOut(?e) :-
    if(at(?e, ?area), not(oiled(?area)),
       linked(?area, ?trap), oiled(?trap), not(ablaze(?trap))),
    do(lure(?e, ?area, ?trap), ignite(?trap)).

% =============================================================================
% METHODS - steps (one plan per companion and skill able to do the step)
% =============================================================================

ignite(?area) :-
    if(canUse(?c, ?skill, fire, ?old, ?new)),
    do(opSpend(?c, ?skill, ?old, ?new), opIgnite(?c, ?skill, ?area)).

spill(?area) :-
    if(canUse(?c, ?skill, oil, ?old, ?new)),
    do(opSpend(?c, ?skill, ?old, ?new), opSpill(?c, ?skill, ?area)).

% The lurer must stand in the trap area: walk there, then lure.
lure(?e, ?from, ?trap) :-
    if(canUse(?c, ?skill, lure, ?old, ?new)),
    do(navigateTo(?c, ?trap),
       opSpend(?c, ?skill, ?old, ?new), opLure(?c, ?skill, ?e),
       opChase(?e, ?from, ?trap)).

% Walk one link at a time along the shortest route (pathNext is native Dijkstra
% over linked/2).
navigateTo(?who, ?dest) :-
    if(at(?who, ?dest)),
    do().

navigateTo(?who, ?dest) :-
    else, if(at(?who, ?cur), pathNext(?cur, ?dest, ?next)),
    do(opMoveTo(?who, ?cur, ?next), navigateTo(?who, ?dest)).
